final.answer: The documentation for FV-2-2 (a Fisher ET/EAT/ETR control valve) lists several available body materials: cast iron, LCC steel, WCC steel, WC9 chrome moly steel, and CF8M (316 stainless steel), with CF3M also mentioned alongside CF8M, plus generic carbon/alloy/stainless steel options. Yes, stainless steel is available for corrosive service — the CF8M (316 stainless steel) body is offered, and 316 CF8M is explicitly listed as a body material option. Note that the exact temperature limits depend on the body/trim combination and bolting, so the applicable combination should be checked against the referenced tables.

**Direct answer:** The trim (cage) options named in the datasheet are the standard cages, Whisper Trim, Whisper NXG Trim, WhisperFlo and Cavitrol III cages, plus the Fisher Trim Cartridge option. The Whisper Trim / Whisper NXG / WhisperFlo trims are the ones for noise attenuation, and the Cavitrol III cage is the one for cavitation protection under high pressure drop conditions.

**Details from the facts:**

- The easy-e valve family's shared features list "aerodynamic noise attenuation of the Whisper Trim/WhisperFlo cages and cavitation protection of the Cavitrol III cages" [p. 2]. In plain words: the Whisper trims reduce the sound the fluid makes as it passes through; the Cavitrol III cage protects against cavitation, which is bubble formation and collapse that happens at high pressure drops.
- For valves with Whisper Trim III and Whisper NXG Trim cages (levels A1 through D3), the maximum pressure drop is limited to 0.999 ΔP/P1 (the pressure drop divided by the inlet pressure — a value near 1.0 means almost the whole inlet pressure can be dropped across the valve). A footnote warns not to exceed a maximum ΔP/P1 ratio for a given cage level, as excessive noise increases if it is exceeded [p. 3, p. 4].
- Figure captions show the physical constructions: "Metal Seat and Whisper Trim III Cage in Fisher ET Valve" and "Cavitrol III One-Stage Cage" [p. 16], "Typical Balanced TSO (Tight Shutoff) Trim" [p. 16], and "Typical Trim for Cavitrol III Cage Constructions" (Figure 14) [p. 19], plus "Typical Trim for All Valves Except Those with Cavitrol III, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim or WhisperFlo Cages" (Figure 13) [p. 18].
- The Fisher Trim Cartridge is offered as a trim option in new valve assemblies or as a repair solution, available in some ET configurations (NPS 1 to 4 full and reduced ports), with fully backward compatibility and the same flow characteristics as comparable traditional trim; it comes with pre-set ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE packing, with ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF and duplex packings also available, and optional PEEK high-temperature anti-extrusion rings [p. 6, p. 7].
- The specification table also lists trims by flow direction and flow characteristic: standard, Whisper Trim, WhisperFlo and Cavitrol cages with linear characteristic, and standard cages with quick-opening, linear or equal percentage [p. 4].

**What I could not find in the facts:** a single sentence that explicitly says "for high pressure drop or noise, use trim X." The closest is the family description naming Whisper trims for noise attenuation and Cavitrol III for cavitation protection [p. 2], and the ΔP/P1 noise limit note for Whisper Trim III / Whisper NXG cages [p. 3–4]. I also could not find the exact list of numbered trims (e.g. 1, 4, 27, 37, 85) as a complete options list — they appear only in notes under Figures 13–15.
